beginner.summary: For backend and full-stack developers who can read JSON and use a terminal but are new to JSON Web Tokens. It covers the structure of a JWS compact token, base64url encoding, registered, public and private claims, HS256 signing and verification, expiry and not-before timing, issuer and audience validation, minting tokens in Node.js and Python, the JOSE header, access versus ID and refresh tokens, browser storage, common validation mistakes and a signed login-flow capstone.
prerequisites: Comfortable reading and writing JSON and using a command-line shell
Can run a small Node.js or Python program and install packages
Understands basic HTTP requests, headers and status codes such as 200 and 401
outcomes: Decode and explain the three parts of a JWS compact token
Mint and verify HS256 tokens enforcing expiry, issuer and audience
Avoid the most common validation mistakes such as trusting the header algorithm
Build a signed login flow with issue, verify and refresh endpoints

Validate tokens correctly in Java, .NET and Go services
